question: When a self-improving search process is allowed to mutate its own proposal generator, does reusing the task evaluator for generator changes produce progressive evaluator capture, and does a structurally separate Generator Gate preserve external coherence without freezing improvement?

mutation_tiers.tier_1: Operational candidate-local mutations. Receipt Gate / E_task.
mutation_tiers.tier_2: Persistent, shared, proposal-shaping, or unknown-surface mutations. Generator Gate.
mutation_tiers.tier_3: E_meta and principal-owned constitutional surfaces. Out-of-band principal authority only.

boundary_laundering_rule: Any persistent/shared/proposal-shaping or unknown mutation surface defaults to Tier 2 regardless of declared tier. Behavioral cumulative proposal-distribution drift independently escalates to Tier 2.

evaluators.E_task: Finite public/common-case suite plus speed utility. Used for operational selection in both arms and generator selection in Arm A.
evaluators.E_meta: Hidden rotating concrete-case suites with per-epoch query budgets. Used only for generator-level changes in Arm B. Generator receives accept/reject plus receipt hash, not score or cases.
evaluators.E_external: Independent terminal-only direct plus metamorphic evaluator. Never queried during adaptive search or generator gating.

positive_control.purpose: Verify that E_task contains a realistic exploitable omission and E_external can detect it.

anti_rescue: After the first primary run, changing evaluator families, scoring weights, query budgets, rotation cadence, candidate space, mutation cadence, seeds, thresholds, or verdict rules requires a new experiment ID.
claim_boundary: A positive result supports Generator Gate separation only on this frozen reference evolutionary code-optimization substrate. It does not establish a universal law of recursive self-improvement, autonomous-agent safety, or real-world swarm behavior.
